The default MIDI channel is 16. Hold FX SELECT to enter CONFIG, select CHANNEL, press FX SELECT to highlight the current channel, rotate to choose a channel and press to confirm.
Use FX SELECT to choose EXIT from CHANNEL, then EXIT from CONFIG. The selected MIDI channel persists when power is switched off.

limitations.message: Coverage limit: MIDI channel configuration and persistence determine the channel for these default-context CC assignments.

Conflicting information: FX-mode table starts at C-2, but the same manufacturer support article maps numeric Note 0 to C-1 in its Octave/Note Numbers and CC/Hex/Note conversion tables. All Note-name bindings are withheld rather than selecting an octave convention.
Not included: Channel FX MODE INT/EXT for A and channels 1–4; Channel FILTER selects A, 1–4 and EXT RTN; Channel CUE selects A, 1–4 and XONE:FX; XONE FILTER HPF/BPF/LPF/ON; XONE:FX PRE/POST, MODE, TAP, ON, CUE and FX X-FADE X/Y; XONE:SYNC BEAT LEFT/RIGHT, BEND LEFT/RIGHT, STOP/PLAY

Conflicting information: The supplemental CC conversion table lists decimal 13/14/15 against 0x0C/0x0D/0x0E. The extracted CC0–11 assignments are outside the erroneous rows; no corrected source values are invented.
Not included: Conversion-table rows 13–15

Coverage limit: The manual says the mixer can send and receive MIDI, but its assignment charts do not specify per-control data ranges, rotary direction encoding, Note release bytes or host feedback values. CC input addresses are retained with empty values; no host-to-device mirror is inferred.
Not included: All host-to-device bindings pending receive semantics; rotary value encoding; Note release semantics

Based on archived manufacturer documentation. The complete extraction metadata, original excluded chart rows and source files are retained in the manufacturer evidence archive. No hardware testing is claimed.
